reuse.why: Builds on the tree's single weekend-rule definition (applyWeekendRule / applyWeekendRuleToDay / getDateWithSkippedWeekend) at every site, and the new range handler reuses applyWeekendRule, recurConfigToRSchedule and the captureBreadcrumb pattern.

duplication.why: Holiday matching exists in two representations (isOffDay's YYYY-MM-DD / MM-DD Set lookup for moves, and recurConfigToExdates' year-by-year expansion for daily skips), and the exdates argument has to be added separately at each of the four RSchedule constructions.

placement.why: The daily skip is expressed in recurConfigToRSchedule and holidays in shared/schedules.ts, so all consumers share it; pairing rrules with exdates is left to each caller instead of one schedule factory.

scope.why: All edits serve the four steps (daily skip, range handler, holidays, yearly holidays) plus release notes.

maintainability.why: The design is centralised, but a % 7 'empty rule' hack, a 60-year exdate expansion around the current year, and the need to remember exdates whenever an RSchedule is built are fragile.

bypasses_abstraction.where: Every weekend/holiday move goes through applyWeekendRule or applyWeekendRuleToDay, and every RSchedule construction in the tree receives recurConfigToExdates.

disguised_duplication.where: The full-date-or-MM-DD holiday rule is implemented once as a Set lookup in isOffDay and again as a date expansion in recurConfigToExdates in shared/schedules.ts.

abstraction_drift.where: A holidays parameter is threaded through applyWeekendRule, applyWeekendRuleToDay and getDateWithSkippedWeekend; recurConfigToRSchedule gains a daily skipWeekend branch plus an interval % 7 weekend-start special case; no call site bypasses the shared rule.
